extract:
Shawn Corey Carter, known professionally as JAY-Z, was born in 1969 and raised in the Marcy Houses, a public housing project in the Bedford-Stuyvesant neighborhood of Brooklyn, New York. He came up in the late 1980s New York rap scene, initially trading verses with local figures like Jaz-O, who served as an early mentor, and briefly appearing alongside Big Daddy Kane on tour. After failing to secure a major label deal as a solo artist, JAY-Z co-founded Roc-A-Fella Records in 1995 with Damon Dash and Kareem "Biggs" Burke, a move born of necessity that would become one of the most consequential independent ventures in hip-hop history.

His 1996 debut Reasonable Doubt, released through a distribution arrangement with Priority, fused mafioso narratives with a luxurious, jazz-tinged sound courtesy of producers like DJ Premier (on Friend or Foe and D'Evils), Ski (Dead Presidents II, Feelin' It), and Clark Kent. It featured a now-iconic verse from The Notorious B.I.G. on Brooklyn's Finest. Though it sold modestly at the time, the album is now widely regarded as a classic. The follow-up In My Lifetime, Vol. 1 (1997) leaned more commercial, working with Puff Daddy and the Hitmen, while Vol. 2... Hard Knock Life (1998) broke him to the mainstream, powered by the Mark the 45 King–produced title track that sampled Annie. Vol. 3... Life and Times of S. Carter and 2000's The Dynasty: Roc La Familia further entrenched his dominance and introduced producers Just Blaze and a young Kanye West to wider audiences.

The Blueprint, released on September 11, 2001, is often cited as his artistic peak, with Kanye West and Just Blaze crafting soul-sample-driven beats on tracks like Izzo (H.O.V.A.), Heart of the City, and the Nas diss Takeover, which escalated one of rap's defining feuds (answered by Nas's Ether). The Black Album (2003), framed as a retirement record, featured Rick Rubin's stripped-down 99 Problems and Timbaland's Dirt Off Your Shoulder, and inspired Danger Mouse's mashup The Grey Album. After a brief hiatus during which he served as president of Def Jam, JAY-Z returned with Kingdom Come (2006) and American Gangster (2007), then partnered with Kanye West for the maximalist Watch the Throne (2011), which produced Niggas in Paris and Otis. His later solo work includes Magna Carta Holy Grail (2013) and the introspective 4:44 (2017), produced almost entirely by No I.D. and addressing his marriage to Beyoncé and infidelity directly.

Beyond music, JAY-Z built Roc Nation into a sprawling entertainment and sports management company, founded the streaming service Tidal (later sold in part to Square), and launched the cognac and champagne ventures D'Ussé and Armand de Brignac. He has won numerous Grammy Awards and in 2021 became the first rapper inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame as a solo artist. He and Beyoncé released the joint project Everything Is Love in 2018 under the name The Carters.

JAY-Z has not released a solo studio album since 4:44, focusing instead on Roc Nation's business operations, the NFL entertainment partnership announced in 2019, and various philanthropic and criminal-justice efforts through the Shawn Carter Foundation and Reform Alliance. His legacy as both a lyricist and a businessman remains foundational to how contemporary hip-hop conceives of artistic and commercial ambition.
